Primary request: Create ONE entirely new wide flattened composite reference for R1 "Rooftops of the Dead City", the upper region of a continuous underwater side-view map. It is visual reference only and must never define topology, collision, a route, landmark placement, or gameplay.
Input images and roles:
- Image 1: material-quality reference ONLY. Borrow premium painterly-realistic surface fidelity, credible cracked concrete, corroded metal, masonry wear, aggregate, tile, and dense hand-authored material texture. Do not copy its diver, HUD, objects, layout, cyan illumination, glow, or atmosphere.
- Image 2: macro layout-guide context ONLY. Use only the fact that R1 is the upper map band and may have a loose broken rhythm of horizontal rooftops or shelf motifs. Do not reproduce its grid, labels, text, boxes, landmark arrangement, terrain silhouettes, or topology.
- Images 3 through 5: flat 2D side-scroll composition and layering references ONLY. Learn their dominant open-water negative space, parallel cutout-like planes, isolated floating props, material attached to cropped terrain edges, and darkest foreground occlusion entering from image edges. Do not copy their HUD, text, numbers, characters, divers, lamps, lighting, creatures, collectibles, exact terrain shapes, exact objects, palette, outlines, or cel-shaded/cartoon rendering.
Scene/backdrop: Submerged uppermost remains of a dead coastal city, represented as sparse front-facing cutout layers: cropped roof parapets, upper-floor facade fragments, broken cornices, thin tiled roof edges, restrained cable loops and rebar. Everything is inert, non-interactive, and disconnected. Cool relatively clear R1 palette: one calm field of dark desaturated blue-green water, slate concrete, oxidized steel, muted mineral grey, restrained matte algae. Preserve readable midtones without highlights.
Style/medium: premium painterly-realistic material rendering placed onto extremely flat graphic 2D planes; orthographic side-scrolling game environment composite; realistic textures but NOT photorealistic cinematic depth and NOT the cel-shaded style of Images 3-5. Matte neutral base plate with no baked atmosphere.
Composition/framing: wide 16:9. EXTREMELY FLAT strict orthographic side elevation, more like layered 2D cutouts than a perspective scene. Every architectural face is front-on or perfect profile. Parallel verticals and horizontals. Zero vanishing point, zero perspective convergence, zero horizon line, zero receding ground or ceiling plane, zero three-quarter view, zero camera tilt, zero lens distortion, zero depth of field. The open-water negative space is dominant: keep approximately 55-65 percent of the full frame calm, empty, and low-detail, including a broad uncluttered center. It is visual breathing space only, never a tunnel, doorway, shortcut, platform, corridor boundary, or playable route. R1 may have broad horizontal rooftop/shelf motifs, but they must be broken, cropped by the canvas edges, discontinuous, clearly decorative, and non-navigable.
Four clearly separable composited visual planes integrated into ONE image, with NO labels, borders, panels, layer diagrams, or text:
1. Far slow-parallax backdrop: a few very large, extremely simplified, low-contrast front-facing silhouettes of distant upper facades, roof tanks without lights, parapets, chimneys, and collapsed rooflines. Flat silhouette blocks only, no perspective, no blur, no fog, no texture noise, broad quiet masses.
2. Isolated floating-prop plane: only 4-7 small, widely separated, inert fragments floating in the open field: a blank broken awning frame, a plain detached railing section, a few masonry or roof-tile fragments, one loose cable loop. Each reads as an independent decorative prop, never a pickup, container, clue, hazard, creature, lamp, or focal object.
3. Collider/SDF-adjacent material plane: thin premium material skins attached only to disconnected, cropped upper and lower boundary fragments. Show cracked concrete, roof tile, mineral aggregate, corroded reinforcement, chipped plaster, and sparse matte algae. These skins must look like decorative surface treatment on an assumed external edge, not an authored landmass; do not connect them into a route, room, tunnel, or closed passage.
4. Dark edge-only foreground overlay: very dark, low-detail occluding shapes ONLY in sparse outer corners and along short extreme-edge sections. Use cropped rebar, cable tangles, broken stone, and parapet fragments. Never form a continuous frame and never enter the central open-water field. This plane must be clearly darker and flatter than plane 3.
Lighting/mood: no depicted light source. Uniform neutral diffuse material visibility and even exposure, restrained local ambient occlusion/contact shading only. No cast-light pattern, no directional light, no highlights, no rim light, no bright focal point, no dramatic shadow cone.
Output intent: one clean flattened 24-bit RGB composite reference with no alpha and no baked global atmosphere or post-processing, suitable as a visual layering target before Godot independently adds water, lighting, motion, particles, refraction, caustics, fog, and color processing.
Constraints: background/reference art only; four planes must remain visibly distinct through flat value grouping, scale, edge attachment, and overlap rather than atmospheric perspective; dominant central negative space; no topology authority; no text or character.
